publication: Artem Chernikov, Lecture Notes on Stability Theory, UCLA MATH 285D Winter 2015, updated 2017-08-27, 54-page author-hosted PDF; printed p. = PDF p.

reviews.checked_passages: Section 2.2 printed pp.11–13: type-counting bounds, Definition2.9 of finite order patterns/stability, Proposition2.10 and the Erdos–Makkai combinatorial argument in Theorem2.13. Section2.4 printed pp.16–19 was inspected for indiscernibility definitions, the Ramsey/compactness construction, and scope boundaries.
reviews.consumers: [Indiscernible sequences](entries/indiscernible-sequences/entry.html) and [Order patterns and stability](entries/order-patterns-and-stability/entry.html). The latter adopts Definitions2.9/Proposition2.10 and gives explicit cut/equality type counts; the Erdos–Makkai proof was inspected for scope but is not adopted in this introduction.
reviews.outcome: CHERNIKOV-ST-01 records the missing distinctness hypothesis in adjacent Lemma2.31. The corpus will require an infinite source for Ramsey extraction, distinguish a newly constructed sequence from a subsequence, and avoid monster-model assumptions in the elementary compactness construction. Later spectra, forking, ranks, and the full characterization theorem are outside the adopted scope. Theorem2.37 and its compressed pattern-selection step were not adopted or certified.
